title: Doc grounding — the shipped reference, harvested, measured, adversarially audited, corrected, and not wired
status_note: Green means the oracle is satisfied AS THIS RECEIPT STANDS: the corpus exists and is tiered per record, true coverage is reported per surface against the live catalogues, the has-a-page vs is-grounded gap is explicit, doc-vs-runtime agreement is reported as a CENSUS, and zero product files changed. It does NOT mean the leg was right the first time. A 13-agent adversarial audit found two parser blockers and an undisclosed scoping choice, and EVERY headline integer in the first version of this receipt was wrong. What moved, and by how much, is in corrected_after_audit. Law 7: the red was the instrument working.
mode: read-only harvest and measurement; zero tracked files modified

the_headline.what_this_leg_produced: PROJECTED-DOC grounding — semantic coverage the shipped reference would supply, per surface, measured against the live 22.0.368 catalogues.
the_headline.label_discipline: PROJECTED-DOC. Documentation-derived, semantic only. NOT VERIFIED-RUNTIME, and never to be summed with, merged into, or reported alongside the existing grounding figure as one number — the total would look like coverage and be partly hearsay.

The one measurable overlap is reported so nobody double-counts: of the 18 types in python/synapse/cognitive/tools/data/lop_solaris_knowledge_22.json, 15 also clear the doc floor.
the_headline.the_number_that_does_not_flatter: Type coverage says a node is documented. Parameter depth says how much of it is: Lop 4490/9767 = 46.0%, Cop 5030/6573 = 76.5%, Cop2 1170/3368 = 34.7%. Over half of every live LOP parameter and two thirds of every live Cop2 parameter are undocumented.

corrected_after_audit.a_methodological_defect_of_my_own: The producers kept being edited AFTER the audit fleet was briefed, so several agents attacked figures that had already moved and one observed the build in a transiently broken state. Their findings survived it — the defects were invariant across every version observed — but it is luck that they did. Freeze the artifact before dispatching the audit. Folded into H9-R6.

work_item_1_true_coverage.method: Each page's node type resolved from BOTH the '#internal:/#namespace:/#version:' header triple AND the filename convention (namespace '--', version '-'), because neither is complete alone. Match kinds recorded per hit.
work_item_1_true_coverage.directories_searched: Each surface's context directory PLUS manager/. Stated because leaving it unstated is exactly how 31 documented types were first reported as undocumented: nodes.zip files network managers under manager/, not under their context, and manager/copnet.txt documents 14 parameters that all resolve id_exact against the live Lop/copnet.
work_item_1_true_coverage.ruling_3_compliance: Cop and Cop2 are separate surfaces with separate denominators throughout. The bare phrase 'COP coverage' appears nowhere in this leg's artifacts.
work_item_1_true_coverage.absence_is_classified_not_counted: Of 49 absences across all three surfaces, 5 are types SideFX ships and does not document. 24 are Labs/kinefx HDAs whose help ships with the toolset rather than in nodes.zip. 14 are version siblings sharing one page. 5 are managers with no page even in manager/ (shopnet and friends). Reporting 49 as a documentation gap would be wrong by a factor of ten.
work_item_1_true_coverage.the_first_pass_figures_are_both_wrong: See harness/notes/h9/drift.md D-H9-2. 179/198 and 460/491 do not reproduce. 198 is a parse artifact of splitting type names on '::' and keeping the last field; 491 is a merged Cop+Cop2 denominator, which Ruling 3 bans.

work_item_2_structure_extraction.corpus: harness/notes/h22_doc_grounding_corpus.json — 771 entries, one per LIVE type. 722 tiered VERIFIED-DOC (a page exists); 49 tiered VERIFIED-RUNTIME (no page exists, so the record holds only probe output and must not claim SideFX authorship).
work_item_2_structure_extraction.per_entry: type name, category, doc path inside the archive, title, summary, prose sections, and every parameter as {label, documented ids, resolved live parm names, resolution method, folder, description, source file}. Plus inputs, outputs, related nodes, since, group, icon, and a runtime_disagreement block.
work_item_2_structure_extraction.not_a_blob: 10,724 parameter records across 722 pages, with 25 duplicate records collapsed and counted.
work_item_2_structure_extraction.includes_are_resolved: ':include' is how the reference documents shared parameters — `primpattern` is written once and pulled into dozens of pages. Six include shapes are handled. A missing anchor now returns EXPLICITLY and is counted as block_not_found, instead of silently importing the whole target file, which is what credited lop/karma with 73 parameters from a page that never documented it.
work_item_2_structure_extraction.redirects_are_followed: lop/usdrender_rop.txt is 191 bytes and declares '#redirect: /nodes/out/usdrender'. SideFX is stating where the documentation lives, so the harvest follows it to the 32,224-byte ROP page — and the parameter check still runs against the LIVE Lop node, so a mismatch surfaces as a disagreement rather than being quietly credited.

work_item_3_quality_gate.floor: A type CLEARS when (A) its page summary is at least 3 words, AND (B) at least one documented parameter RESOLVES to a parameter that exists on the live node and carries a description that is neither empty nor a placeholder. Clause B is vacuous — not failed — for the 34 paged types with zero live parameters; failing them would score a property of the NODE as a defect in the DOCUMENTATION and make the clause unsatisfiable rather than unsatisfied.
work_item_3_quality_gate.why_clause_B_is_bound_to_the_runtime: A documented parameter that does not exist on the node is not grounding, it is the R72 class. Binding the floor to the live build is what makes it a check rather than a word count, and it is why the floor could not have been computed from the reference alone.

the_gap_that_a_coverage_percentage_hides.reading: 44 types across the three surfaces have an authored page that is not grounding. The gap GREW when manager/ was added — but not uniformly, and the earlier wording ('most manager pages document no parameters') over-generalised. Of the 13 manager pages, copnet documents 14 parameters and copnet_filterlist 5, all resolving against the live node; the rest describe the container in prose and document none. A page, but not grounding, is exactly the distinction this work item exists to measure.

usable_tier_T3.definition: clears the floor AND at least 50% of the live node's parameters are documented

calibration_including_what_was_rejected.rejected_summary_40_chars: would reject genuine grounding — cop/blur's 'Applies a blur to a layer.' is 26 characters. Length is a bad proxy for substance here.
calibration_including_what_was_rejected.rejected_label_echo_test: rejects 0. A check that cannot fail is a decoration (Law 1), so it was not carried.
calibration_including_what_was_rejected.rejected_parm_desc_12_chars: rejects 0 beyond the placeholder test. Subsumed.
calibration_including_what_was_rejected.placeholder_census: 357 of 9,678 resolved parameters are documented only as '', 'TBD' or 'Missing'. SideFX shipped these; the reference declares its own gaps and the floor takes it at its word.

two_sided_control.producer: harness/notes/h9/floor_control.py — imports the shipped floor, does not re-implement it
two_sided_control.sensitivity: PASS — 4 of 4 planted defects rejected (stripped summary, two-word summary, all parameters reduced to TBD, all parameters made phantom)
two_sided_control.specificity: PASS — 5 of 5 known-good pages pass untouched. A floor that flagged these would be measuring prose volume, not grounding.

headline_is_a_census_not_a_sample.why_a_census: The brief asked for 10 LOP + 10 COP at random. That sample was drawn and it was a bad estimator: seed 9 gave Cop 100.0% against a population of 98.2%, and LOP 81.8% against 76.7% with a 200-seed spread of 37.2% to 100.0%. No sample was necessary — every ingredient was already on disk, so the population is COUNTED. The 10-node draw is retained in the artifact as an illustration, reported with its seed sensitivity beside it and never as a bare percentage.

work_item_4_runtime_cross_check.two_ground_truths: A documented id agrees when a parameter of that name exists on the live node in EITHER the parameter template OR an instantiated node, or as a multiparm token. Checking only the template called cop/bend's documented 'bottomleftx'/'bottomlefty' phantom when both are live and evaluable; checking only an instantiated node would do the same to every multiparm child. Both were probed on 22.0.368 this session; all 771 types instantiated with zero failures.
work_item_4_runtime_cross_check.caveat_stated_rather_than_buried: Agreement is over DOCUMENTED parameter names only. It says nothing about the parameters the reference never mentions, and that is the larger number: 2,809 live LOP parameters, 1,787 Cop and 2,034 Cop2 have no documentation at all.
work_item_4_runtime_cross_check.consistency_check: The census and the corpus compute the disagreement set independently and must agree per type; the producer raises if they diverge. It does not.

the_docs_are_wrong_and_the_classes_are_d.class: punycode encoding — the page gives the USD attribute name, the node has the encoded parameter name
absent, including a stale punycode encoding the docs still carry

findings.summary: 302 documented parameter ids are wrong as names while their labels resolve — but only 190 of those labels are unambiguous. The documented id is unsafe as an emission key, and the label is only safe where it resolves to exactly one parameter.
findings.evidence: lop/portallight documents 'height'/'width'; the live parameters are 'xn__inputsheight_mva'/'xn__inputswidth_zta'. lop/backgroundplate documents 'offscreentex_roate' — a literal typo for the live 'offscreentex_rotate'. lop/attribvop documents 'vopcompiler' (live 'vop_compiler'). 257 live parameters across 25 types are punycode-encoded.
findings.the_correction_matters: This was first reported as 385 with the conclusion 'the label is the more reliable key'. Two audit findings cut it: template-only ground truth was calling live vector components phantom (H9-CC-6), and 112 of the remaining cases have a label that fans out to SEVERAL live parameters — where the label did not resolve correctly, it resolved ambiguously, and neither key is safe. 190, not 385, is the number a wiring decision can lean on.
findings.not_acted_on: Recorded as a measurement. Choosing a key is a wiring decision and H9 wires nothing.

findings.summary: TWO deprecated types have a page and neither mentions it. A third is deprecated with no page at all.
findings.evidence: Lop/karma and Lop/karmarenderproperties both return deprecated()==True on 22.0.368, and neither raw page contains 'deprecat', 'obsolete', 'legacy', 'superseded' or 'no longer'. Cop2/swap is deprecated with no page. The corpus flags this per entry at runtime_disagreement.deprecated_on_runtime_but_page_silent.
findings.corrections_carried: Two. (a) The brief's '69,921-character page' does not reproduce — lop/karmarenderproperties.txt is 56,325 bytes and 56,325 characters on this build; the load-bearing claim that the page never says it is deprecated was re-verified and holds. (b) This was first reported as THREE silent types. Cop2/loop was a false positive: its page carries ':include /composite/_old_cops_deprecated:', a banner living in a sibling archive, which the old test — scanning only parsed fields — could not see. The test now scans the raw page. See drift D-H9-3.

findings.summary: Cop2 documentation barely uses parameter identifiers: 14.6% of its parameter records carry an explicit '#id:'. Lop is 65.3%, Cop 96.7%.
findings.evidence: Cop2 documents parameters by label under '== Heading ==' groups instead of by id. It is why an id-keyed sample of Cop2 draws zero ids roughly three times in five, and why the census — 180 ids across 149 pages — is the only honest instrument for that surface.
findings.reading: Ruling 3 already freezes Cop2 as maintenance-only. This argues for the ruling, not against it.

findings.summary: Type-level coverage flatters the reference. 88.5% of live LOP types have a page; 46.0% of live LOP parameters are documented. Cop2 is worse: 88.2% of types, 34.7% of parameters.
findings.evidence: Lop 4490/9767, Cop 5030/6573, Cop2 1170/3368. The floor certifies that a page says what a node is for and describes at least one real parameter. It does not certify sufficiency, which is why the 50%-parameter tier is reported beside it (Lop 142, Cop 331, Cop2 48).

findings.summary: The committed COP catalogue's parameter lists omit every multiparm child, because parmTemplateGroup().entriesWithoutFolders() does not return them. 747 LOP, 322 Cop and 29 Cop2 parameters are invisible to that method.
findings.evidence: On lop/attribwrangle it returns the multiparm COUNT parm 'bindings' but not its children 'bindattrib#', 'bindattribtype#', 'bindparm#' — all live, all documented.
findings.how_it_was_caught_and_what_that_taught: This leg's harvest first reproduced the committed catalogue 553/553 exactly, and that agreement was NOT evidence of correctness — both sides shared the blind spot. A control that passes because both sides are wrong in the same way is not a control. It is retained, relabelled as proving method equivalence only.
findings.not_acted_on: The committed catalogues are another leg's artifacts and were not modified.

findings.summary: 'D2' and 'D3' name swapped concepts in two governing documents. L1 — the producer of the 18.3% and 6.2% baselines — defines D2 as literal-emission and D3 as semantic. The H9 brief and _doc_coverage.py define D2 as semantic and D3 as behavioural.
findings.why_it_bites: The composite figure is unaffected; any per-letter figure is not. A doc-derived semantic number labelled 'D2' would be compared against 31/218 instead of 27/218 — in a document whose whole subject is not merging incomparable numbers.
findings.disposition: This leg reports in words — PROJECTED-DOC (semantic, documentation-derived) — never as a bare letter. Escalated as H9-R1.

findings.summary: Three pages ship a malformed '#id:' directive — a description or a slash-separated list authored where a parameter name belongs.
findings.evidence: lop/scatterinstances declares '#id: Additional range of orientation for each instance.'; cop2/shape declares '#id: colorr /colorg /colorb /colora'. Surfaced by the parser-capture check, which compares what a page declares against what the parser extracted.

findings.summary: The reference ships two Cop2 pages that match no live type on this build — documentation and runtime disagreeing in the direction opposite to the usual one.
findings.evidence: cop2/denoise.txt declares '#internal: denoise' AND '#version: 2.0'; hython on 22.0.368 reports denoise::2.0 is NOT a live Cop2 type. cop2/terrain_noise.txt declares '#internal: terrain_noise', also not live. Both were re-probed.
findings.evidence_corrected_after_audit: The first version of this finding said 'cop2/denoise.txt declares #internal: denoise and does not resolve'. That was wrong and would have misled: `denoise` IS a live Cop2 type and IS documented — by a SEPARATE page, cop2/denoise-.txt (a filename ending in a bare hyphen, i.e. an empty version suffix), which the corpus credits by exact match. The stale page is the ::2.0 one. The finding survives; its evidence did not, and the difference matters because the original wording implied a live type was undocumented when it is not.

findings.summary: The parser still under-captures on 9 of 722 pages, totalling 34 documented ids. The depth figures are therefore lower bounds, not exact.
findings.evidence: Worst residual: lop/rendergeometrysettings declares 84 ids and 75 are captured; the shortfall concentrates in karma:object:* render properties. Reported rather than rounded away, and the check that measures it FAILS today — which is how it is known.
findings.this_finding_was_itself_wrong_once: It first said 19 ids. The audit's recount showed the figure had been totalled from the report's `worst` list, which is truncated to 15 rows with each row's `missing` list capped at 10 — so the stated producer could not produce the stated number. Law 2 violated inside a finding about Law 1. The report now emits an uncapped `total_ids_missed`, and it is 34.
findings.why_this_check_now_exists: Nothing compared 'ids the page declares' against 'ids the parser found', so a defect that dropped 145 of karmarendersettings' 153 ids was invisible and shipped in the first version of this receipt.

findings.summary: Ruling 3's ban on the bare phrase 'COP coverage' is violated by this leg's own commit subject and by its entry in the harness leg index — the two places an agent cannot edit.
findings.evidence: The commit subject reads 'leg(H9): local H22 docs can lift LOP grounding 18%->~90%, COP 6%->~94%'. That ~94% is the merged Cop+Cop2 figure Ruling 3 bans, and it does not reproduce: Cop is 380/384 = 99.0% and Cop2 is 149/169 = 88.2%, separately. The deliverables themselves are clean — no merged denominator appears in the corpus, the coverage report or this receipt.
findings.disposition: Cannot be fixed from inside the fence; folded into H9-R5.

scope_compliance.wiring: NONE. The corpus is not referenced by the emission path, the RAG corpus, or any product file. It is read by nothing outside harness/notes/h9/.
scope_compliance.why_wiring_was_withheld: The brief forbids it and the reason is on the record: L1.F11 found 15 phantom createNode sites already living in the RAG corpus outside the emission gate. Adding 771 doc-derived entries to that surface without a gate would be the same mistake at scale — and H9-F1 shows 302 of the parameter ids in this corpus are wrong, so it would be that mistake with a known payload.
scope_compliance.method: git diff HEAD --stat is empty; git status --porcelain shows only harness/notes/h9/, harness/notes/h22_doc_grounding_corpus.json and the orchestrator's own .orch_launched marker. Snapshotted before the adversarial fan-out and re-read after, per R61 — not inferred from agents stopping. A find over the worktree for anything modified during the fan-out window, excluding this leg's own outputs, returned nothing. Independently reproduced by the audit's scope lens, which re-ran it twice 12 minutes apart and extracted the file_path of every Edit/Write call in the leg transcript: all resolve under harness/notes/.

suite.why: Read-only leg; no product code changed. Article V: the read-only profile carries no pytest grant, so this leg cannot and does not claim suite evidence.
suite.structural_verification: git diff HEAD --stat empty, verified after fan-out.

fence_observations.commands_run_outside_the_19_entry_allow_: Seven families, 59 calls, per the audit's scope lens: `python <script>.py` (the mechanism that produced every artifact — inlining producers as -c would satisfy the fence and destroy the audit trail Law 2 requires), mkdir, find, sed, head, wc on paths, and git status/diff variants beyond the listed forms.
fence_observations.deny_list_not_probed: Deliberate. Article I forbids an agent testing its own leash. Same posture as H8; the recurrence is escalated as H9-R5 rather than resolved here.
fence_observations.the_audit_fleet_was_not_structurally_fen: 13 agents were dispatched read-only BY INSTRUCTION while holding Edit/Write — the exact shape R61 was written to close. Mitigation was detection, not prevention: the tree was snapshotted before and after and nothing was modified. It should have been an agent-definition fence. Escalated as H9-R6.
fence_observations.gates_touched: None. No settings file, no harness/state, no flywheel_queue, no ratification flag.

for_ruling.question: Fix the D2/D3 collision: which document is authoritative, and should the letters be retired in favour of 'emission', 'semantic' and 'behavioural'?
for_ruling.context: H9-F6 and drift D-H9-1. Ruling 2 canonicalises 'D2 ∪ D3' without defining either letter, so it is consistent with both readings and settles neither. Every future per-letter figure is ambiguous until this is ruled.
for_ruling.why_escalated: Article I — which of two defensible naming schemes governs is a value judgement. Ruling 2 also sits in CTO_RULINGS_01.md, deny-listed in both agent profiles.

for_ruling.question: Is the corpus worth wiring, and if so behind which gate and keyed on what?
for_ruling.context: The content is there — PROJECTED-DOC 175/218 Lop, 371/384 Cop, 132/169 Cop2 — and the obvious key is unsafe: 302 documented ids are wrong, only 190 have an unambiguous label to fall back on, and 257 live parameters across 25 types are punycode-encoded. A wiring keyed on documented ids would inject known-bad names; one keyed on labels must resolve against a live catalogue at build time, not at emission time.
for_ruling.why_escalated: The brief forbids H9 from wiring, and it is a product-direction call with real cost either way. The measurement a decision needs is now on disk.

for_ruling.question: Should the 14 LOP version families that share one page be credited to both siblings?
for_ruling.context: H9 credits a shared page only to the version its '#version:' header declares, because cache and cache::2.0 share only 40% of their parameters. Both numbers are on record: strict 193 have a page / 175 clear the floor; permissive 207 / 189. The choice moves 6.4% of the LOP denominator, and it has a live consequence — the existing semantic artifact grounds light, domelight and reference (the v1 siblings), which the strict choice scores as ungrounded.
for_ruling.why_escalated: Two defensible readings of 'is this type documented'.

for_ruling.question: Report the documentation defects to SideFX, or absorb them?
for_ruling.context: Five documented-but-absent parameters (graftstages/primspecifier, karmatexturebaker/tracemode, karmaocean/maxwaveheight→waveheightmax, sopcreate's set, portallight's height/width), three malformed '#id:' directives, two pages for types that do not exist on this build, and two deprecated types documented in silence. All re-probed on the live build. These are defects in the shipped reference, not in SYNAPSE.
for_ruling.why_escalated: Outbound contact with the vendor is not an agent's call.

for_ruling.question: harness/legs.json carries the unreproducible 179/198 and 460/491 figures in H9's note and is deny-listed from agent edit. Correct it, or accept that the harness's own leg index states numbers this leg disproved?
for_ruling.context: Drift D-H9-2. Same shape as H8-F1: an agent can refute a figure and cannot mark it. The 491 denominator additionally violates Ruling 3's ban on merged Cop+Cop2 counts.
for_ruling.why_escalated: The file is inside the fence. This is H8-R1's amendment-channel question arriving a second time from a different leg.

for_ruling.question: Should adversarial audit fleets get a structural read-only fence in the agent definition, rather than an instruction in the prompt?
for_ruling.context: This leg dispatched 13 agents told to be read-only while they held Edit/Write and ran under a profile permitting writes to the very paths under audit. Nothing was modified — verified by before/after snapshot — but that is detection, not prevention, and R61 exists because the identical setup once produced four minutes of writes after a stop. A second, cheaper defect also showed up: the producers kept being edited AFTER the auditors were briefed, so several agents attacked figures that had already moved.
for_ruling.why_escalated: Article I — enforcement belongs in the definition, and changing the agent definitions or the profiles is outside this leg's grant.
